text:
Calgary's week turned on a hit. Chicago's Wyatt Kaiser was suspended three games for his hit on Martin Pospisil, per Sportsnet, and Pospisil's status was uncertain heading into Monday in Ottawa. The Flames lost that one 2-1, their third straight without a win (0-2-1), and they've been outscored 10-5 in the run.

The skid is mostly earned. Calgary has 46% of the expected goals this season (the quality of chances) and 45% over its last 10, and by our standings model its points match its play almost exactly. At 10-13-2, the Flames score 2.44 goals a game and allow 3.44. The power play produces 0.41 expected goals a game, they take more penalties than they draw, and the goals are running about eight behind the chances.

There are young reasons to keep watching. Jonathan Castagna scored his first two NHL goals in a win in San Jose, and The Win Column is already asking whether the Flames struck gold. Zayne Parekh and Yan Kuznetsov have been the best pair by chances (54%), while Jake Middleton and Zach Whitecloud have been outscored 13-9 at 5-on-5. Simon Nemec scored on the rush against Minnesota, with an unlikely assist from equipment manager Ben Dumaine, per Sportsnet.

Our playoff odds have Calgary at 7%. What we'd watch: how Ryan Huska fills Pospisil's spot beside Ryan Strome and Matvei Gridin if he misses time, and whether the kids keep getting minutes.
headline: Flames keep sliding as Pospisil waits
